section_summary: This section records U.S. and Far Eastern Commission decisions on Japanese industrial capacity and the selection, allocation, and delivery of plants as reparations. It includes directives to SCAP, correspondence about Korea’s exclusion from advance transfers, and proposals for financing Japanese production. Later papers dispute the scope of a Strike Corporation survey and possible unilateral U.S. action, while Burma seeks sugar factory machinery.

subfiles.title: Annex to appendix: comparisons of recommended retained levels of industry
subfiles.about: Compares proposals for retained capacity across Japanese industries.
subfiles.summary: Lists assured, present, proposed, interim, and agreed capacity levels for metals, chemicals, machinery, power, shipping, petroleum, and other industries.

subfiles.title: Request for Korean share of Japanese reparations
subfiles.about: Asks that Korea receive industrial equipment from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kim argues that Japanese machinery, iron, and steel would relieve Korean unemployment and inflation, and seeks a Korean share of future reparations.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to Yongjeung Kim
subfiles.about: Explains why Korea was excluded from advance transfers.
subfiles.summary: Says Korea may receive part of the eventual U.S. share.

subfiles.title: Revised reply to Yongjeung Kim
subfiles.about: Restates the U.S. position on Korean reparations.
subfiles.summary: Promises consideration of Korea’s economic needs in allocating the U.S. share.

subfiles.title: Reply to Yongjeung Kim
subfiles.about: Declines Korea’s request for advance reparations transfers.
subfiles.summary: Cites the emergency relief directive’s scope and promises to consider Korea in final disposition.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Directive No. 75
subfiles.about: Forwards three copies of a directive sent to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Designates copies for the Far Eastern Commission and State Department files.

subfiles.title: Directive No. 75: advance transfers and allocation procedures
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets advance transfer limits and procedures for Japanese industrial reparations.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes limited advance deliveries to China, the Philippines, the Netherlands for the East Indies, and the United Kingdom for its affected territories. It prescribes inventories, valuation, claims, allocation priorities, recipient accounts, technical missions, and removal deadlines. SCAP retains authority over plant allocations and unresolved disputes.

subfiles.title: Filing Directive No. 75 with the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Submits a certified copy of Directive No. 75.
subfiles.summary: Files the directive under the Commission’s terms of reference.

subfiles.title: Financing self-liquidating projects for Japan
subfiles.about: Urges dispatch of a cable on privately financed Japanese production.
subfiles.summary: Seeks SCAP’s response so other Far Eastern Commission countries can be invited to participate.

subfiles.title: State Department position on SWNCC 236/44
subfiles.about: Opposes renewed approval of largely settled reparations provisions.
subfiles.summary: Proposes an amendment allowing SCAP temporary retention of facilities essential to occupation needs.

subfiles.title: Private financing of production in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests War Department concurrence in inquiries about Japanese production using imported materials.
subfiles.summary: Uses a proposed soda ash transaction to introduce broader private financing and production arrangements.

subfiles.title: Draft cable on private financing of Japanese production
subfiles.about: Seeks SCAP’s views on supplying raw materials for Japanese manufacture.
subfiles.summary: Proposes repayment in goods or export proceeds across several consumer industries.

subfiles.title: Compilation of reparations removal procedures
subfiles.about: Requests review of a consolidated directive for industrial and shipping reparations removals.
subfiles.summary: Identifies minor additions and revisions to previously approved procedures.

subfiles.title: Manual of reparations procedures
subfiles.about: Explains the proposed handling of a consolidated reparations manual.
subfiles.summary: Anticipates War Department dispatch and withdrawal of SWNCC 236/44.

subfiles.title: Disposition of attached SWNCC paper
subfiles.about: Reports that an April 29 decision made action on an attachment unnecessary.
subfiles.summary: Records concurrence that no further action is needed.

subfiles.title: Query on SWNCC 236/44 action
subfiles.about: Asks whether an attachment remains appropriate after the April 29 decision.
subfiles.summary: Requests Martin’s view on further action.

subfiles.title: Consolidated draft directive on industrial reparations removals
subfiles.about: Consolidates existing instructions on selecting, allocating, and delivering Japanese industrial facilities.
subfiles.summary: The draft covers plant selection, inventory, valuation, competing claims, accounting, delivery costs, title transfer, transport, time limits, and technical missions. It balances claimant preferences with Japan’s peacetime needs and gives priority to removal of war related and zaibatsu facilities. It also addresses destruction, restitution claims, occupation needs, and disputes.

subfiles.title: Record of preparation of consolidated directive
subfiles.about: Explains why a consolidated SCAP directive was prepared.
subfiles.summary: Lists provisions added or clarified from earlier policy papers.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about SCAP cable CM-IN 4343
subfiles.about: Asks whether a February SCAP cable requires a State Department reply.
subfiles.summary: Reports conflicting recollections about responsibility for answering the cable.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning sulfuric acid, whaling, and light metals
subfiles.about: Responds to proposed interpretations of Japanese industrial retention policy.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring rejects blanket exemptions for integrated sulfuric acid plants and whaling vessels, finding occupation retention authority sufficient. He supports clearer language on aluminum and magnesium but rejects a permanent exemption for nonferrous rolling capacity. He urges a revised message to MacArthur and flexibility in Far Eastern Commission negotiations.

subfiles.title: Electric furnace steel capacity in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests War Department concurrence in a cable seeking SCAP’s steel capacity assessment.
subfiles.summary: Seeks evidence for extending temporary electric furnace capacity and explaining limited removal designations.

subfiles.title: Request to clear electric furnace capacity cable
subfiles.about: Calls for urgent clearance of a draft cable to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Explains the need for SCAP’s figures before Far Eastern Commission negotiations.

subfiles.title: Draft cable on electric furnace capacity
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP’s preferred retained electric furnace capacity and removal schedule.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether temporary retention beyond June 30 is needed.

subfiles.title: Copy of memorandum on electric furnace cable
subfiles.about: Repeats the request for urgent clearance of the SCAP cable.
subfiles.summary: Seeks SCAP’s evidence on electric furnace capacity and removals.

subfiles.title: Copy of draft electric furnace cable
subfiles.about: Repeats questions about electric furnace retention and further designations.
subfiles.summary: Requests capacity figures for the final reparations program.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission transmittal of plant selection policy
subfiles.about: Forwards a policy decision on selecting Japanese plants.
subfiles.summary: Requests a directive to SCAP and notification when received in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Certification of Far Eastern Commission decision
subfiles.about: Certifies the attached decision against the original.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the copy is correct.

subfiles.title: Selection of plants for reparations removals, destruction or retention
subfiles.about: Sets criteria for selecting Japanese plants for removal or retention.
subfiles.summary: Prioritizes war related and zaibatsu facilities while balancing claimant needs with Japan’s peacetime economy. Specifies treatment of neutral and United Nations property.

subfiles.title: Draft directive on selection of plants
subfiles.about: Requests forwarding of a draft plant selection directive to the Joint Chiefs.
subfiles.summary: Also requests acknowledgment so the adopted policy can be released publicly.

subfiles.title: Draft directive implementing plant selection policy
subfiles.about: Implements the Far Eastern Commission’s May 22 plant selection decision.
subfiles.summary: Directs SCAP to consider industrial disarmament, claimant and Japanese needs, zaibatsu ownership, and United Nations property.

subfiles.title: Chemical Industries of Japan report
subfiles.about: Sends a requested Foreign Economic Administration report.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the April 1945 chemical industry report.

subfiles.title: Moscow report on Eden and Lancashire textiles
subfiles.about: Reports a Soviet allegation about opposition to restoring Japanese industry.
subfiles.summary: Says a Moscow commentary attributed Eden’s position to Lancashire textile interests.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Directive No. 80
subfiles.about: Forwards three copies of the plant selection directive sent to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Assigns one copy to the Commission and two to State files.

subfiles.title: Filing Directive No. 80 with the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Submits a certified copy of Directive No. 80.
subfiles.summary: Files the plant selection directive under the Commission’s terms of reference.

subfiles.title: Directive No. 80: selection of plants
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs SCAP to apply Far Eastern Commission plant selection criteria.
subfiles.summary: Gives preference to removing war related and zaibatsu facilities while weighing claimants’ needs against Japanese peacetime requirements. It sets ownership priorities and refers United Nations property to a separate decision.

subfiles.title: Program of Strike Corporation in Japan
subfiles.about: Challenges a War Department message claiming State endorsement of broad unilateral action.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring asks whether the Strike report will cover more than reparations plant selections and retentions. He rejects the implied State endorsement of unilateral action on reparations, recovery, and a peace treaty. He seeks a corrected message to MacArthur and a copy of the Strike contract.

subfiles.title: Allison memorandum on unilateral reparations action
subfiles.about: Warns that unilateral U.S. reparations decisions could damage Commission relations.
subfiles.summary: Quotes McCoy’s warning that extensive interim directives might threaten the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.title: Martin memorandum on Petersen–MacArthur message
subfiles.about: Questions an unapproved assertion of State support for the Strike mission program.
subfiles.summary: Urges clarification with Petersen before the mission departs.

subfiles.title: Revised memorandum on Strike Corporation program
subfiles.about: Seeks correction of a message suggesting State approved unilateral Japanese policy.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring questions the Strike mission’s scope and any delay to economic recovery or peace treaty work. He urges Petersen to tell SCAP that State did not approve the disputed paragraph or to issue a jointly endorsed correction.

subfiles.title: Request for sugar factory machinery for Burma
subfiles.about: Seeks Japanese reparations machinery for a former sugar factory near Mogaung.
subfiles.summary: Recommends assistance and asks that the request be relayed to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Reply on Burmese reparations request
subfiles.about: Directs Burmese officials to pursue Japanese reparations through Britain.
subfiles.summary: Explains that Burma’s claim is handled as part of the British claim.
